Managed as data (an operator file or admin surface), versioned, and never inferred from co-occurrence alone. 2e070f4f: the map is configuration — [fandom_graph] version + edges{from,to,weight}, validated at load (self-loop, weight outside (0,1], NaN, unnamed end, empty version each refused naming the edge). domain::fandom_graph::FandomGraph answers neighbours()/expand() with symmetric closure, strongest-weight-per-pair (weight AND spelling, so line order cannot change the map), threshold applied once, seeds never returned. db::fandom_graph::related_works returns (work, fandom, weight, likes) for published/public works in the named fandoms, ordered by weight then likes, seed excluded. STILL MISSING, and why the row stays planned: tag.cross_fandom and author.similar have no route in this build — the registry lists them and nothing serves them — so the map is reachable via the door and related_works, not yet via those two surfaces. open_requirements.requirement: taste gravity applies at every recommendation surface as a bounded influence layer after the blend, with a per-surface strength, reordering and never filtering
open_requirements.notes: PARTIAL 71adfa72 (first half): taste gravity is now a convex mixture served=(1-g)*base+g*taste, both terms normalised to 0..=1 over the page; unbounded multiplier replaced. Reorders never filters (same length/elements asserted); the algorithm's own score is NOT rewritten; stable ties; egalitarian mode still switches it off. Per-surface strength via [taste] gravity_per_surface + gravity_ceiling (refused outside 0..=1 at load, and it bounds the number in force including the global value) + gravity_locked; TasteConfig::strength_for(surface). The feed publishes gravity{mode,strength,moved_up,moved_down,unchanged} - mode and a coarse pull, never a score or per-item reason. NOT DONE: story.similar / library.because_you_shelved and the other registry surfaces have no candidate pipeline to pull on, so discover.feed and the concierge (`home.curated`) honour the layer (1f05deff); taste_signal SHIPPED f74bd400: darkhold_db::taste_signal::for_account scores each candidate by the share of ITS canonical entities that appear on the works the account has shelved (share of the candidate, not of the shelf); absent from the map = unmeasured, Some(0.0) = measured and cold, None = no shelf at all; wired on both gravity surfaces. Ratings would be a better input and are not stored per reader (work_ratings holds an aggregate mu/phi/sigma), which is named in the module. END-TO-END f52beefd: a shelved reader's feed ranks the work sharing the shelf's tag above one sharing nothing at pull 1.0 (mutation: inverted affinity reddens it), and the published pull is now measured at the END of the pipeline (PullHistogram::between) because M45's taste ordering moves rows after gravity and the mid-pipeline histogram said 'nothing moved' on a page whose order had changed. Still missing: the surfaces without a candidate pipeline (story.similar, library.because_you_shelved). the reader's dial SHIPPED c9e4527d: migration 0171 reader_gravity + GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/discovery/gravity, narrowing only (refused above the instance, out-of-range refused not clamped, locked refuses with the lock named, DELETE clears rather than storing 0.0, stored values clamped on read), and the feed applies it; the gravity block reports strength (in force) beside instance. Original note: P9. served = (1-g)*algorithm + g*taste_match, taste_match from the operator profile (§16.2) over fandom/tag/author/source. Default g = 0.15; story.more_by_author = 0.0, story.similar = 0.10, home.trending = 0.35. Constraints: reorders never filters (M43-02), floor/ceiling are configuration (§16.16's shape), the reader's dial reaches zero unless locked (§16.5), no per-item reason is printed and no score is exposed (§0.3) while the mode and a coarse pull histogram are published, and gravity is measured as its own experimental arm so 'it helped' is a number.

open_requirements.requirement: both identity gates see the spellings the schema actually uses: bare `account`, `created_by`, `pseud_id`
open_requirements.notes: Measured 2026-11-02 while closing M45-62, from the migrations rather than from memory: 68 identity-carrying columns sit outside the foreign-key graph, and neither gate can see 37 of them. `scripts/check-snapshot-pii.py`'s IDENTITY_NAME_RE matches account_id, user_id, owner_id, author_id, actor_id, e-mail/password, token/secret/api_key, ip, user_agent, real name, phone, address, lat/long, device_token, endpoint, session_id, cookie, fingerprint — and not a bare `account`, not `created_by`, not `pseud_id`. `crates/db/tests/erasure_covers_fk_free_accounts.rs` matches account_id, *_account and *_account_id — and not a bare `account` or `created_by`. So 25 bare `account` columns (taste_profiles, dashboard_layouts, group_members, conversation_participants, presence, wishlists, event_participation, trust_levels, sanctions, operator_role, credit_entries, credit_holds, subscriptions, usage_counters, extension_grants, push_subscriptions, ai_requests, privacy_requests, reader_work_progress, forum_throttle_log, exchange_terms, ...) and 12 `created_by` columns (challenges, events, bounties, translation_jobs, announcements, directory_lists, categories, category_proposals, entry_moderation_proposals, taxonomy_edges, ...) are decided by nothing but habit. The fix is not "add a regex alternative": both gates compare measured against classified in BOTH directions, so widening the pattern turns them red until all 68 columns carry a treatment, and each treatment is a judgement (pseud vs account vs public handle) that has to be read off the writer — RequirePseud or RequireSession in the handler that inserts the row. That inventory IS the ticket; the regex is one line of it. Second finding, fixed already and worth keeping: the snapshot gate was not in CI at all, so it had been red in a clean tree since M47-14 with nothing to notice. It runs now (.github/workflows/ci.yml).

open_requirements.requirement: Every db listing query that a reader surface depends on is either wired to a route or deleted: no function exists only to satisfy its own test.
open_requirements.notes:
Found while implementing M70-12 and confirming it with a live probe. `content::list_public_works_by_freshness` is called by nothing in crates/app — its only callers are crates/app/tests/publication_events.rs and the M70-12 test — so the ordering guarantees it asserts (event-log `new` vs `updated`, NULL publish events sorting last) are proven about a function no reader can reach. Two honest ends: wire it into the home/freshness feed (and check whether the feed that exists today reproduces those guarantees), or delete it and move the ordering assertions onto the SQL that does serve. The probe that surfaced it: /api/v1/works?sort=new is the AUTHOR's list and answers AUTH_REQUIRED to a stranger, and the stranger's feed comes from browse.rs, not from this function. RATCHET 2026-11-06 (f19ecf18): crates/app/tests/orphan_queries.rs fails when a NEW db function is reachable only from tests; baseline in docs/plans/orphan-queries.txt, generated by scripts/orphan-queries.py (294 orphans measured today); a second test fails when the list names a function that no longer exists. ROW STAYS PLANNED: the requirement is every listing query wired or deleted, and 294 are neither. The named case in this row (content::list_public_works_by_freshness) IS wired - the landing page reads it (8a51f9de). Next step for the row: work the baseline down crate by crate, starting with the archives/import surfaces where a wired route is the honest end and a deletion would lose an operator capability.

PROGRESS 2026-11-08. The ratchet's list was 15 at the first full gate run of this session; it is 11 now, and the four it lost went three different ways, which is the point of the triage in docs/plans/m70-13-orphan-triage.md:
* `accepted_holder` and `fork_manifest` had no caller anywhere and were DELETED.
* `assert_tag` was a writer with no door, and now has one: `POST /works/{id}/tags/{node}/assert`, beside `…/confirm` and `DELETE /works/{id}/tags/{node}`, on the `taxonomy` module (crates/app/src/routes/tag_assertions.rs). Four HTTP tests on each engine; four mutants red — proposals shown to everyone, a wrangler confirmation without the operator, anyone allowed to retract, and ownership assumed rather than derived.
* `keybind_holder` was mine (M69-21) and was inlined into the writer that needed it.
**The detector under-reports.** `reachable_sources` concatenates every non-test source and matches with a plain `contains`, so `confirm` passed on `confirm_plan`, `retract` passed on prose, and `assertions_for_work` passed on a doc comment in tag_inference.rs — three functions with no caller at all, declared reachable by a comment. The scan needs a whole-identifier match (`assert_tag(` rather than `assert_tag`); until it has one, a green run means less than it says. REMAINING, 11: internal helpers whose `pub` is wrong (`accepted_holder_anywhere`, `find_notice`, `find_assignment`, `arm_totals`, `clear_override`, `install_override`, `velocity_signals`) and writers with no door (`holds_grant`, `seller_net`, `snapshot_day`, `active_grants`).

CORRECTION 2026-11-08: I first recorded that the scan used a plain `contains`; it did not — it required an identifier boundary and accepted any whole-identifier occurrence, so a doc comment (`assertions_for_work`), a local binding (`confirm` in erasure.rs) and an unrelated route handler (`cta::retract`) all satisfied it. Requiring `(` after the name took the list from 11 to 30, and the nineteen it added are real: each was measured and appears in crates/app only as a local variable, a JSON key, or a same-worded route function -- never a call. FOURTEENTH PASS 2026-11-08: record_inbound now has its caller. POST /federation/inbox stores the activity and also writes an intake row, quarantined, with peer_host taken from the actor id (object_id from the object, or the actor when the activity has no object; a non-URL actor records 'unknown' rather than dropping the evidence). Decisions: quarantined is not a decision (the door accepts accepted|rejected only, so a row's decision cannot be erased without erasing the row); the note is optional on either answer (a refusal that needs a sentence to be recorded is a refusal made without recording it); quarantined_in_page counts the page and says so; a filter outside the vocabulary is 422 not everything; a caller without operator standing gets 404 (ADR 0030). A ledger write that fails does not fail the request — the activity is stored and the peer is waiting, and a bookkeeping fault turned into a refusal makes them retry and double-writes. Proof: m70_13_federation_intake 1 test on SQLite and PostgreSQL, two mutants red (peer host not extracted; state guard disabled), route_inventory 5 with two rows, milestone_43_federation 21, milestone_18 7, clippy clean, gate ok. Signature verification (draft-cavage Signature header, Digest, actor key fetch) is the next unit on this surface.

FIFTEENTH PASS 2026-11-08: the inbox verifies HTTP signatures (ADR 0031). New module crates/app/src/http_signature.rs implements draft-cavage rsa-sha256: the Signature header must cover (request-target), host, date and digest; Date within five minutes; Digest matched per entry (multi-algorithm headers are legal, RFC 3230); the peer key comes from its actor document and is cached per keyId (fragment stripped for the fetch, kept for the cache), and a failed fetch is not cached. Config [federation] require_signature defaults TRUE and that default is the decision. Ledger state is now the answer to 'was this verified': verified -> accepted with the key id in the note; refused -> rejected before the 401 is returned (probing is visible); unsigned with the requirement off -> quarantined, so 'verified' and 'allowed' never collapse into one word. An unparseable Signature header is refused, never treated as absent. Proof: m70_13_inbox_signature 2 tests on SQLite and PostgreSQL with a real 2048-bit RSA keypair (accepted; tampered body; subset covered headers; stale date; unknown key; unsigned both ways), 4 unit tests, four mutants red (digest off, covered-header rule off, freshness off, unsigned accepted), milestone_43_federation 21, route_inventory 5, config_sections 13, clippy clean, gates ok, docs/config-reference.md documents the section. Named limits: authority is the actor document fetched over TLS (every AP implementation's assumption), a separate publicKey.id document is not followed, hs2019-with-Ed25519 refused by algorithm name. INCIDENT: a mutant-clearing `git checkout crates/app/src/routes/federation.rs` discarded the uncommitted signature wiring in that file; it was re-applied from the same session and re-verified. Lesson repeated: copy the file to /tmp before mutating, never `git checkout` in a dirty tree.

open_requirements.requirement: Browse, search, library and the overflow view of every recommendation rail render results as dense list rows — title, author, provenance word, word count, unit count, completion, rating, date, metrics — with a stated total and cursor pagination, never a card grid and never infinite scroll.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 2, no new backend. 141,317 catalogue rows behind a card grid is the strongest finding in the external design and the cheapest. Sorts stay the closed vocabulary; sort changes order and never hides results (§8.1). Row height consistent; quick actions on hover/focus, always visible on mobile.

open_requirements.requirement: The operator console becomes its own visual register: dense rows, monospace values, red/amber/green status with a word, an alert bar naming every red state with a 'fix' link, 404 for non-operators, and no component shared with the reader-facing site that would soften a failure.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 3. §8.20 made operational: the console is allowed to be less beautiful than the reader and is not allowed to hide a red state. Today the ~30 admin surfaces use the same component library as the reading site. Acceptance: the admin overview renders each group from live counts and every warning has an action; a non-operator gets 404.

open_requirements.requirement: The reader gains an auto-hiding bar (back, unit navigation, position, typography, bookmark, in-work search) and a typography panel whose settings are per reader and per work, with provenance shown ('your default' / 'instance default' / 'this work') and a reset at each level.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 2, additive to the existing server-rendered reader. Typography must stay independent of the site theme (§4.11 of the proposal); the panel offers font family including a dyslexia-friendly option, size, line height, measure in characters, justification and four functional presets. Acceptance: settings survive a device change; an RTL work and an LTR work do not share them; the panel renders without JS as a form.

open_requirements.requirement: Reader position is honest: a position recorded against an older revision is reported as stale and offered as a choice, two devices that disagree are offered as a choice, and a position with no reliable evidence renders '—' rather than a false 0%.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 3. The anchor system exists; the honesty layer does not. §8.14 and §8.17 make silence and silent overwrite both bugs; §11 forbids fake precision. Acceptance: three tests, one per state, each asserting the choice text and that no percentage is fabricated. f3aca3fc: domain::reading::ResumeState has four states — current / stale / unmeasured / conflict — each with its own sentence, and percent() is Option<u16> so only `current` carries a number; display() renders '—' otherwise, which is what makes 'no measurement' unable to become '0%' in a template. AGREEMENT_PERMILLE = 50: a slider moved a pixel is not a second opinion. A recorded revision whose unit is gone is stale with current: None (an anchor cannot be honoured), not current. db::reading::positions_with_current_revision joins each stored row to the revision its unit points at NOW in one statement, so the answer is about one moment; GET /api/v1/reading/progress publishes `resume: {state, percent, display, sentence, needs_a_choice}` beside the existing positions/resolution, and the raw rows still travel so a page can offer the stale place as a choice. The deeper bug fixed on the way: save_progress recorded the revision ONLY when the client sent content_revision, so a browser that omits it owned a position that could never be detected as stale — it now resolves the unit's current revision server-side when the client is silent, while still recording an older client-sent revision as the real stale case. STILL MISSING: the reader's bar and the choice UI; the API states all three cases.

open_requirements.requirement: Facet counts are a server capability with a latency budget: one endpoint returns counts per facet value under the current filter set, the UI renders them per group and shows '—' while they update, and the p95 stays inside the budget on the 141k-row catalogue.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 3, and the most underpriced item in the external design: no route in the 720 returned a facet count — STALE: /api/v1/facets has returned counts per facet value since M64-10 (one scan, four facets, when_unknown), and /api/v1/facets/words since M71-12 (grep '"facets"' crates/app/src is empty). This is an aggregate query plan — indexes, a cache, a budget — not a component. Acceptance: a load measurement with the decision rule fixed before the run, documented in the row. Remaining work is therefore the UI half (per-group counts, the '—' pending state) and the p95 measurement on the 141k catalogue with the decision rule fixed before the run; the aggregate endpoint itself is not the gap. DECISION RULE, fixed 2026-11-07 before any run (recorded in advance so it cannot be chosen after the numbers): target GET /api/v1/facets with no filters — the four-facet aggregate — against the live darkhold catalogue on thinkcentre (58,042 works, 141,317 library_items, 30,982 work_tags), requested 50 times sequentially from the host over 127.0.0.1:8081 after 5 warm requests, one token cookie, no other load. PASS iff p50 <= 100 ms AND p95 <= 200 ms AND every response is 200 with four facet groups; FAIL otherwise, in which case the measured numbers go in this row and the next step is indexes/caching, not a re-run with a looser bar. 41e847e4 MEASURED, rule pre-registered at 82db6c0e before any run: 50 sequential requests after 5 warmups on the live catalogue (58,042 works / 141,317 library_items) -> 50/50 200 but p50 297 ms, p95 372 ms against a budget of p50<=100 / p95<=200 = FAIL. EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) ruled out the index answer: three sequential scans (works 58,042; units 127,474; revisions 127,474) + a 12.5 MB external-merge sort for one group aggregate, 235 ms before the sort and 398 ms total — facets are O(catalogue) by construction. Fix: crates/app/src/facets_cache.rs memoises the answer per (database, filter set) for 60 s, bounded at 256 entries with TTL eviction; both facet-bearing endpoints publish computed_at_ms_ago and the facet door publishes cache_ttl_seconds, so the staleness bound is part of the contract rather than a hidden property. The database is part of the key because a filter string alone does not say whose catalogue it counts — a test process opening one database per test served one test's counts to another and went red on exactly that. clear() exists for an operator action that must see its own write. RE-MEASURED after deploy: warm p50 2.83 ms / p95 6.05 ms / max 7.36 ms over the same 50-request sequence; the pre-registered rule as written PASSES on that sequence, and the honest reading is that the sequence is warm — the cold path is stated separately (1,174 ms first request after restart, ~300 ms steady-state scan), not averaged in. ALONG THE WAY, two production-breaking defects in the same scan, invisible to the SQLite-only tests: (1) SUM(bigint) is NUMERIC on PostgreSQL so `GET /api/v1/facets` answered every live request 500 with `mismatched types ... SQL type NUMERIC` — fixed with a per-backend ::BIGINT cast, guarded by crates/db/tests/facets_two_engines.rs; (2) the scan built `?1`,`?2` placeholders and handed the raw text to sqlx on both engines, so EVERY FILTERED facet request failed with `operator does not exist: ? integer` on PostgreSQL — the statement now goes through Database::sql and uses bare `?` (with `?1` the rewrite produced `$11`), with CAST(? AS BIGINT) so the window bound has a type. STILL MISSING: the UI half — per-group rendering and the '—' pending state while counts update.

open_requirements.requirement: The word-count filter is a real histogram: a distribution endpoint returns ten buckets for the current filter set, the control draws them and lets a range be selected over the bars, and the selected bounds are stated as numbers.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 4, depends on M71-11's aggregate surface — same query shape, different grouping. Decorative bars fed by invented data are forbidden (the proposal is right that the histogram must be real). 9fd5955a: the distribution endpoint exists — GET /api/v1/facets/words?tag=&q=&buckets=&min_words=&max_words=&max_rating= returns 10 population-equal buckets (quantile edges, not equal width: equal width puts 8 of 10 skewed works in one bar) with low/high/count/share, plus measured/unknown/total/when_unknown over the same filtered set the facet route describes. Unmeasured rows (a unit with no current revision — this schema has revisions.word_count NOT NULL, so that IS the unmeasured state) are excluded from every bucket and counted in unknown; buckets partition the measured set exactly once, ties included; empty buckets are dropped and the rest renumbered so a chart has no gaps. STILL MISSING for the row: the control that draws the bars and lets a range be selected over them, and M71-11's latency measurement.

open_requirements.requirement: Every surface that enumerates a partially covered dimension states its coverage: the fandom facet leads with 'N of M works are tagged (P%)', fandom and source pages split hosted from referenced, and the numbers come from one aggregate view rather than being typed into copy.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 3. 5.4% fandom coverage is a fact the CLI already prints and the UI hides; a catalogue that hides it is claiming a completeness it does not have. Acceptance: the numbers on a page equal a query's output, asserted in a test. bf404997: db::taxonomy::dimension_coverage(dimension, value) computes the view count and the published+public catalogue count in ONE statement (two round trips could report a share of two different archives) and builds the sentence there, so no two surfaces phrase the same gap differently. Three cases: works>0 → '2 of 5 works in this archive are tagged slow burn (40.0%)'; works==0 with a non-empty catalogue → 'No published work in this archive is tagged X any more' (a dimension page exists because something carried it, so zero means the rows went away; 0.0% is true and useless); empty catalogue → 'nothing to measure against'. Wired on /api/v1/tags/{tag} and /api/v1/fandoms/{fandom} as `coverage` + on the DOCUMENT tag page (its bare '12 works' replaced), because the document is the surface a crawler and a JS-off reader sees. STILL MISSING: the facet panel's 'N of M works are tagged (P%)' leading line is a UI claim (the API already publishes known/unknown/total per facet). a7664d54 closes the collection half differently from the tag/fandom half, on purpose: a collection is a hand-picked set, so events::collection_coverage counts entries vs readable entries INSIDE it (published+public+undeleted) instead of against the archive, publishes hidden as its own number, and has three sentences — '2 of 5 entries are readable; 3 entries are private, unpublished or deleted.', '2 entries, all of them readable.', 'This collection has no entries yet.' The remaining M71-13 item is the facet panel's leading 'N of M works are tagged (P%)' line, which is a UI claim: the API already publishes known/unknown/total per facet and coverage on tag, fandom and collection.

open_requirements.requirement: Settings show inheritance with provenance at every level (instance, account, pseud, per-work), deep-link to the exact control, offer a reset at each level that overrides, and reflect inline changes made elsewhere with a 'set as default' affordance.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 4. The product already has per-work reader overrides and content filters enforced server-side; the settings surface does not explain where a value came from, so an override looks like a bug. Locked chips for server-enforced filters carry a link to settings and no dismiss control (§8.16). b799f828: GET /api/v1/settings/privacy now carries `provenance` (account keys) and `pseud_provenance` (per pseud), each {value, source: SettingSource (instance|account|pseud), reset: {method, path, becomes} | null, note?}; source reuses darkhold_domain::settings::SettingSource so /settings/export and this door cannot spell a level differently. New door DELETE /api/v1/settings/privacy/{key}[?pseud_id=] clears one level (204 whether or not a row existed; 422 on an unknown key; 404 on a pseud that is not yours — deliberately not 403, which would be an account-enumeration oracle). THE FINDING: registration and pseud creation write every key at account/pseud scope by design, and those rows were indistinguishable from choices, so a fresh account reported six settings as its own decisions and a later instance-default change could never reach it — migration 0180 adds privacy_settings.origin ('onboarding'|'reader', default 'reader' so pre-existing rows keep their meaning rather than being relabelled by a guess); onboarding writes 'onboarding', every reader write writes 'reader', and an onboarding row is reported as instance with a note and no reset. This reverses the earlier in-code claim that the difference 'is not actionable'. STILL MISSING: the per-work level, the deep link to the exact control, and typography/gravity settings are not yet reported through this vocabulary.

open_requirements.requirement: The query string and the facet panel are one state: every facet is expressible in the grammar, or it is rendered as a visible chip that cannot be dropped by editing the string — no filter may disappear because it had no field.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 3. The query grammar has no fields for provenance, source or language; a design that presents the string as the state would silently drop those filters, which is hidden state the product forbids (§8.2 closed vocabulary, §8.14 named degradation). 6c35aee9: the ledger's premise was wrong about which facet was missing. Language has a field; the RATING CEILING did not, and it is the one filter every search page has — the route applied max_rating while the grammar could not spell it, so editing the string dropped the filter from view with the filter still in force. Fix: ValueKind::Rank + QueryField::Rating comparable, RATING_RANKS (general<teen<mature<explicit) in query.rs read by both parser validation and the renderer's CASE (text comparison would order by spelling, not by the product's judgement); unknown names refused with the vocabulary listed. New crates/domain/src/filter_state.rs: FilterState{text,min_words,max_words,max_rating,sort,pinned} with canonical query_string() (no `sort:` — writing a field the parser does not know produces a string that no longer parses), chips() where expressible parts are editable_in_query+removable and pinned parts are neither and carry the reason, unexpressed_note() naming them in words, and from_query_string() so a client does not reimplement the grammar. GET /api/v1/search now returns state{query,chips,unexpressed_note} beside filters and facets, with the reader's content filters as pinned chips (kind = the filter's own type). Also removed ideas rows M63-37/M63-38 from crates/domain/src/modules/ideas.rs and docs/ideas-catalogue.json — both had become implemented-locally-tested and the idea-catalogue test was red; scripts/ideas_catalogue.py refuses to run here because two vault source files are absent, so the removal was by hand to match its output. STILL MISSING: the panel that renders the chips is UI; provenance/source filters have no route, so when they exist they join `pinned` with their own reason.

open_requirements.requirement: The remaining document-class pages migrate in ADR 0006's order - work page /works/{id}, fandom and tag pages, search results, author and collection/series pages - each shipped as server-rendered HTML whose content, links and primary action work with no script, with its Svelte route deleted in the same commit and a server test asserting the no-JS content.
open_requirements.notes: Opened by M71-01 (8a51f9de), which shipped the landing page. Order and reasons are in docs/adr/0006-one-binary-two-renderers.md. The work page is next and is the one that matters for link previews and crawlers: it needs the public view (works::public_view) plus a session-aware split, because the SPA work page carries the signed-in actions (bookmark, kudos, author tools) - a signed-in reader keeps the application, an anonymous one gets the document. Acceptance per page: a test that fetches the HTML, parses it and asserts the content with no script execution, plus a live probe; the Svelte route is removed in the same commit so the count only goes down. PROGRESS 50635a36: landing page (8a51f9de) and work page /works/{id} shipped as documents, each with a no-script test and a live probe. The work page uses reading_decision_publishing_metadata, answers every denial with one 404 page (bodies compared byte for byte in the test), shows a restricted work's record and withholds its text, and hands a signed-in reader the application per ADR 0006. REMAINING per ADR 0006's order: fandom and tag pages, search results, author page, collection and series pages - each deletes its Svelte route in the same commit. TAG PAGE ed9c7088: GET /tags/{tag} is a document listing the works behind a tag (query filters published public works; empty tag = 404 page; capped at 50 with 'more than 50' rather than a false total). The document shell moved to routes/document.rs at the third caller and work_page's copy was deleted. REMAINING: search results, author page, collection and series pages; then delete the Svelte routes for the pages already served as documents.

open_requirements.requirement: One JSON error envelope across the estate's APIs: `{"error":{"code","message","request_id"}}`
open_requirements.notes: Measured today: darkhold `{error:{code,message,request_id}}`, ascend `{error:{code,message,details}}`, kindred `{error:{code,message}}`, ficnexus `{"err":-1,"msg":…}`. Align ascend (add `request_id`, keep `details`), kindred (add `request_id`), and ficnexus behind a documented alias: `err/msg` stays emitted for one release while `error.code` becomes the field clients branch on (config switch `[api] legacy_error_alias`, default on until the exporters' clients move). Proof: one test per service asserting the exact body; a live probe of 8081/8024/8030 with the same `jq -e '.error.code'`; mutant = drop `request_id` from a handler and the probe reddens.

open_requirements.requirement: One meta and health contract: `/api/v1/meta` names the product, version, build, api version, environment and base URL; `/healthz` answers `{status,version}`
open_requirements.notes: Measured today: darkhold answers a full meta document, kindred 404s at `/meta` and puts budgets in `/health`, ascend answers `{status:ok}` at a root `/healthz` and 404s at `/api/v1/meta`, ficnexus mounts `/api`. Every service moves to `/api/v1` (ficnexus keeps `/api` as an alias), answers the same meta shape and the same health shape; product-specific numbers (kindred's algorithm budget, darkhold's policy block) stay as an extra object beside the common fields, never instead of them. Proof: the estate probe in `estate/scripts` reads one expression across the three live ports; mutant = rename `api_version` in one service and the probe fails.

open_requirements.requirement: `@polaris/ui` is adopted by darkhold, then kindred, then ascend, and each adoption is proved by deleting the local component
open_requirements.notes: Order is by size (darkhold 103 svelte files, ascend 40, kindred 14) and by risk (darkhold already imports the kit, so its adoption is a rewrite of imports; kindred's 14 files are small but its skin is the product; ascend's Tailwind markup is the largest mechanical change). Adoption means the local file is removed in the same commit — `git log --diff-filter=D` names it — and the page still renders, checked headlessly, not by a component unit test alone. A product mid-adoption runs two systems; that state must not be committed across more than one row.

open_requirements.requirement: A family navigation module: one component renders `more from this maker` from `estate/generated/nav.json`, by group and tier, replacing hand-written footers
open_requirements.notes: The injected topbar already lists every site, but nothing says which products are siblings: `nav.json` carries `group` (content: darkhold, kindred, suki; social: ascend, gravity, …), `tier` (sfw/nsfw) and `status`. One component in `@polaris/ui` reads that document, shows the same-group siblings, and degrades to nothing when the document is absent — the topbar's own contract. Replaces per-product footer lists. Proof: block `/estate/nav.json` and the module renders nothing; serve a filtered document and exactly the same-group siblings appear; a nsfw page must not link a sfw sibling above the tier line.

open_requirements.requirement: One auth story recorded as a matrix: polaris-id OIDC wherever accounts exist, and an explicit refusal where they do not
open_requirements.notes: darkhold signs in through polaris-id (OIDC + session cookie + bearer for machines); ascend runs its own cookie session with CSRF and no OIDC; kindred has no accounts on purpose (`web/src/lib/session.js`: history stays in the browser); ficnexus has none. Row = `docs/plans/estate-auth-matrix.md` naming each product's answer and one code change: ascend's session becomes a polaris-id client, or the refusal is written down with its reason. Proof: the matrix exists and every row cites the file that implements it; a stranger's request to each product's account door answers the same shape.

open_requirements.requirement: A family design review that runs as a gate: every surface rendered at two widths and in every palette, with the checklist the four products must share
open_requirements.notes: One script renders each product's key pages (darkhold `/`, `/works/{id}`; ascend `/`, `/gallery`; kindred `/`, `/works/{id}`) at 1280 and 390 px, in each palette, headlessly; `estate/ui/a11y.mjs` measures contrast and the script asserts the shared checklist: a visible `:focus-visible` ring, `prefers-reduced-motion` honoured, empty/error/loading states present in the same words, one type scale, no horizontal overflow, heading order. Output committed under `docs/design/family/`. Proof: the script fails on a page with an unstyled `<button>` (the measured 2026-10-27 defect); mutant = remove the focus ring from one component and the gate reddens.

open_requirements.requirement: One noun, one URL: the work page is `/works/{id}` in every product that has one, and one blurb component lists a work the same way
open_requirements.notes: darkhold and kindred already agree on `/works/{id}`; ascend calls the same noun a fic (`/fics/…`) and ficnexus has no page. Row = a vocabulary table in `docs/plans/estate-coherence.md` and the small code changes it implies (ascend keeps `/fics` as a redirect to its canonical path, or the deviation is written down with its reason), plus one `WorkBlurb` in `@polaris/ui` that both darkhold's card frame and kindred's AO3 blurb render through, so the same fields appear in the same order everywhere. Proof: the same work fetched from two products shows the same field set in the same order; a link followed from one product to the other lands on a 200.
